instruction:
Write a t27 spec in the module dialect, module `commands`, that specifies the whole surface of the `tri` CLI so the runtime can be generated from it. House conventions apply: a leading comment banner ending in the `phi^2 + 1/phi^2 = 3 | TRINITY` line, and section banners of `=` comment rules.

Declare `pub const Command = enum(u8)` with exactly seven variants: SpecCommand, GenCommand, CompileProjectCommand, GitCommand, LintCommand, SkillCommand, HelpCommand.

Specify these entry points, all returning i32 (0 success, 1 failure): `spec_create(name, kind)` rejecting an empty name and any kind outside feature/bugfix/hotfix/recovery, and refusing to clobber an existing `specs/<name>.t27`; `spec_validate(spec_path)` enforcing the TDD contract (at least one test or invariant block) and the ADR-004 language policy (no Cyrillic outside docs paths); `spec_list()`; `gen_spec(spec_path, backend, emit_conformance)` which validates before generating and dispatches to zig/c/verilog; `gen_all(backend)`; `compile_project(output_dir, backend)` as a three-pass compile — build a module map from `specs/**` and `compiler/**`, resolve `use X::Y` per file, write outputs plus `build.zig` for the zig backend; `lint_file(path, strict)` and `lint_all(strict)`; `skill_begin(issue_id, kind)`, `skill_seal()`, `skill_status()` over `.trinity/skills/registry.json`; and `help(command)`.

Add the supporting types (Spec, TestBlock, InvariantBlock, Skill, SkillMetadata, SkillRegistry, Conformance) and a fixed-capacity `ModuleMap` struct with init/put/get/count plus `path_to_module_key`, `backend_extension` and `strip_prefix` helpers.

Finish with module-level test, invariant and bench blocks covering the return codes, the rejected inputs, the module map round trip, the path helpers, the seven-variant enum and the latency of spec_create, spec_validate, gen_spec and skill_begin.

Write a t27 spec in the module dialect, file-scoped `module enrichment::youtube_transcript;`, that specifies YouTube transcript extraction as a fallback when NotebookLM cannot ingest a YouTube URL directly. Use the SPDX header and the `phi^2 + 1/phi^2 = 3 | TRINITY` banner.

Constants: VERSION, MAX_TRANSCRIPT_SIZE of 10 MB, YOUTUBE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS 60, YTDLP_CHECK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS 10, and a YOUTUBE_DOMAINS array covering youtube.com, www., m., music. and youtu.be.

Define an `ErrorCode` enum with Success = 0 and distinct non-zero codes for YtDlpNotFound, VideoUnavailable, NoSubtitles, TranscriptTooLarge, InvalidYouTubeUrl, TranscriptTimeout, EncodingError, ApiAuthFailed, NetworkError and UnknownError = 99. Define structs YouTubeSource, Transcript (video_id, title, text, lang, size_bytes) and EnrichmentReport (counters plus an error list).

Specify `is_youtube_url(url) -> bool`; `extract_video_id(url) -> Option<str>` handling youtu.be/ID, the shorts/, embed/, live/ and v/ path forms and the `?v=` query parameter; `srt_to_text(srt) -> str` stripping timestamp lines and standalone line numbers; `extract_transcript(url) -> (Transcript, ErrorCode)` which shells out to yt-dlp with --skip-download --write-subs --write-auto-subs, classifies stderr into VideoUnavailable or NoSubtitles, and enforces the size limit; `upload_transcript(notebook_id, transcript, api_token) -> ErrorCode` posting base64 content to the Discovery Engine `:addSource` endpoint and mapping 401/403 to ApiAuthFailed; and `enrich_with_transcripts(...) -> EnrichmentReport` that skips non-YouTube URLs and accumulates per-URL error messages.

Cover URL detection, every video-id form, and SRT filtering in tests; add invariants for the size limit, non-empty domain list and error-code signs; add benches for the two URL helpers and srt_to_text.

Write a t27 spec in the module dialect, `module HybridArithmetic`, describing a dual-mode big integer for ternary computation: packed storage (5 trits per byte) for memory, unpacked storage (one i8 per trit) for compute. Import base::types, base::ops and numeric::gf16 rather than redefining anything; say so in a comment.

Declare `pub const StorageMode = enum(u8) { packed_mode, unpacked_mode }` and `pub struct HybridBigInt` with packed_data, unpacked_data, mode, sign and trit_count. Add platform-agnostic SIMD vector types Vec32i8 ([32]i8) and Vec32i16 ([16]i16), noting the register mapping is an implementation detail.

Declare — as signatures only, each with a doc comment giving semantics and big-O complexity — zero(), ensureUnpacked(), add(), addSimd() (using Vec32i8, O(n/32)), sub(), mul(), dotProduct() returning i32, pack(), unpack(), createPacked() and createUnpacked().

Then write the TDD section. Tests must use the given/when/then form and cover: zero's sign, count and mode; ensureUnpacked both transitioning and being a no-op; additive and multiplicative identities; sub from zero negating the sign; addSimd agreeing with add; dotProduct positive for identical vectors, zero for orthogonal and negative for opposite; pack/unpack transitions and round trip; the two constructors; add overflow; and commutativity and distributivity of mul. Add invariants restating those algebraic laws and the enum/vector shapes, and benches measuring cycles for add, addSimd, sub, mul, dotProduct, pack, unpack, zero, ensureUnpacked and both constructors.

Write a t27 spec in the module dialect, `module spec_commands`, covering the `tri spec` subcommands with TDD enforcement. No SPDX line; open with a two-line comment naming the file and its purpose.

Specify three pub entry points returning i32: `spec_create(name, path)` which rejects names that are not lowercase alphanumeric with underscores, defaults the output to `specs/<name>.t27`, refuses to overwrite an existing file (pointing at --force), writes a TDD template and then prints numbered next steps; `spec_validate(path)` which reads and parses the file, prints every parse error with line and column, runs `validate_tdd_compliance` on the AST root, and on success prints a summary of constant count plus test and invariant counts for both the spec-style and assembly-style sections; and `spec_list()` which globs `specs/**/*.t27` and marks each file ok or x depending on whether it has tests.

Add helpers `is_valid_spec_name`, `generate_spec_template(name)` — emitting an assembly-style template with `.use base::types`, `.const`, `.data`, `.code`, and `.test`/`.invariant`/`.bench` sections plus a "TDD Contract" comment — and `validate_tdd_compliance(ast_root)` returning the violation list when no test or invariant block exists anywhere.

Declare the AST types it needs: Program, Constant, TestSection, TestCase, InvariantSection, Invariant, SpecDecl, TestBlock, SpecInvariant, ParseError, and a ParseContext with a `has_errors()` method.

Put the test, invariant and bench blocks at file scope after the module, using Zig-style `try std.testing.expect`. Cover the return codes, valid and invalid names, template contents, and both branches of validate_tdd_compliance.

Write a t27 spec in the module dialect, file-scoped `module provider-transform;`, specifying message-format transformation between AI providers. Import Message, MessageRole, MessageContent, ContentType, Tool and ProviderType from provider-schema, and usize from tritype-base. Use the SPDX header and the `φ² + 1/φ² = 3 | TRINITY` banner.

Constants: MAX_HISTORY_LENGTH 100, MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH 100000, and a default system prompt.

Types: `TransformDirection` enum(u8) with anthropic_to_openai = 0 through openai_to_openai = 3; `ContentTransform` enum(u8) identity, escape_tool_calls, unescape_tool_calls, normalize_images; `ParameterTransform` enum; and structs TransformResult, MessageMapping, ToolMapping, TransformOptions, BatchTransformResult, TransformError and TransformedMessage.

Functions: constructors for options, direction (derived from a source/target ProviderType pair), result, error result, mappings, TransformError and TransformedMessage; `transform_messages` looping over a message slice; `transform_single_message`; `map_role` switching on direction with per-direction role maps (note that Anthropic's `tool` role folds into `assistant` going to OpenAI); `transform_content` honouring the normalize_content flag; the four normalize/convert leaf functions; `transform_tools` and `transform_single_tool`; `needs_transformation`; `transform_direction_to_string`; and `is_transform_success`.

Write the TDD section using Zig-style `test "..." { ... try std.testing.expect(...) }` blocks for each constructor and predicate, `invariant` blocks using `@compileAssert` to pin the enum ranges and the positive length constants, and `bench` blocks that loop 1000 times over the cheap constructors with stated cycle targets.

Write a t27 spec in the module dialect, `module ForwardPass`, describing a minimal VSA-based forward pass for LLM inference. Import base::types, numeric::gf16 and ternary::packed_trit and state in a comment that existing specs must be referenced, not duplicated.

Public constants: HEAD_COUNT 3, FORWARD_VERSION 2, ROLE_DIM 500, CONTEXT_WINDOW 8, HEBBIAN_CHARS 95, HEBBIAN_OFFSET 32, MAX_REFINE_PASSES 3.

Types: `RoleVector` (role_id, name, vector as PackedBigInt), `HyperVector` (data, dim) and `ForwardOutput` (output plus an optional loss).

Declare these as signatures only — no bodies — each preceded by a comment restating the signature, what it does, and its complexity: singleHeadAttention, multiHeadAttention (three heads merged via bundle3), forwardPass (v2.29 single head), forwardPassMultiHead (v2.30), resonatorTrainStep returning f64 loss, refineDirectRole, summarizeContext (permute then bundle the 8-vector context), computeDirectRole, directDecode, generateWithDirectRole, buildHebbianCounts returning a HEBBIAN_CHARS x HEBBIAN_CHARS u16 matrix, and hebbianLookup.

Then a TDD section: given/then tests for the attention result, the summarized dimension, decode length and the Hebbian counts and lookup; invariant blocks that document the dimension, matrix-size, context-window and version constraints; and bench blocks that use `@setEvalBranchQuota(10000)` with stated cycle targets for each of the attention, forward-pass, summarize, decode and Hebbian operations.

Write a t27 spec in the module dialect, `module GF20`, defining GoldenFloat20 — a 20-bit phi-structured floating point format. Tag it NUMERIC-STANDARD-001 in the header and import numeric::goldenfloat_family and numeric::phi_ratio.

Layout: 1 sign bit, 7 exponent bits, 12 mantissa bits, EXP_BIAS 63; document the bit map in a comment and record PHI_DISTANCE (the exp/mant ratio's distance from phi) as a constant under 0.04. Store the value as `struct GF20 { raw : u32 }`.

Specify `encode(f32) -> GF20` and `decode(GF20) -> f32` with subnormal handling, the format-property functions max_value, min_positive and epsilon, a `validate_format()` that cross-checks the entry in goldenfloat_family, and a MEMORY_RATIO_VS_FP32 constant of 20/32. Because the spec must be self-contained, also provide the numeric helpers it depends on: floor_log2, extract_mantissa, clamp, a `pow` doing binary exponentiation for integer exponents and exp(y·ln x) otherwise, `ln_approx` via the (x-1)/(x+1) odd series to the 7th term, `exp_approx` via an 8-term Taylor series with range reduction by 5, and `floor`.

Write the TDD section in given/when/then style: zero decode and round trip, the bit-count sum, positivity of the format properties, the phi distance and memory ratio, format validation, then the full battery for pow (zero, one, positive and negative integer, fractional, zero base, one base), ln_approx (1, e, negative → NaN), exp_approx and floor. Add invariants pinning each layout constant and the algebraic identities, and benches with nanosecond targets for pow, ln, exp, floor, encode and decode.

Write a t27 spec in the module dialect, `module GammaConjecture`, formalising conjecture GI1 — that the Barbero-Immirzi parameter of loop quantum gravity equals phi^-3. Import math::constants for PHI and PI. Every claim carries an ID and a tolerance tag in a comment (CONJECTURAL, EMPIRICAL_FIT, or REFERENCE with N/A).

Constants: GAMMA_PHI = pow(PHI, -3.0) as claim C-gamma-001, noting its algebraic forms sqrt(5) - 2 and 1/(2*phi + 1); GAMMA_LQG_STANDARD = ln(2)/(pi*sqrt(3)) after Meissner 2004; GAMMA_LQG_ALT from the Ghosh-Mitra black-hole-entropy fit; and the two relative percentage deltas DELTA_GAMMA_1_PHI_PERCENT and DELTA_GAMMA_2_1_PERCENT.

Formulas, claims C-gamma-002 to C-gamma-006: newtons_constant_from_gamma(gamma, pi) = pi^3 * gamma^2 / phi; black_hole_entropy_from_gamma(gamma, area) = gamma * area / pi; black_hole_shadow_from_gamma(gamma, mass, radius) = 3*sqrt(3)*gamma*M/r; and two superconductor critical-temperature variants SC3 (gamma^2/pi * scale) and SC4 (gamma*pi/phi * scale).

Add a `GammaConjectureReport` struct and `verify_gamma_conjecture(area, mass, radius, scale)` that fills it with both gamma values, both deltas, the two Newton predictions and the two entropies.

Then a TDD section in given/and/then form: that gamma_phi matches all three algebraic forms to 1e-12 or better, that the LQG standard value reproduces its closed form, that delta_1_phi lands between 0.6 and 0.7 percent while delta_2_1 lands between 13 and 14.5, that delta_2_1 exceeds ten times delta_1_phi, and that every formula is positive on unit inputs. Mirror the key claims as invariants and add nanosecond benches for the report and each formula.

Write a t27 spec in the module dialect, `module Axi4`, defining the AXI4-Lite and AXI4-Full bus interface for the Trinity T27 FPGA HIR. Keep the description parser-compatible: flat arrays plus count fields, no nested aggregates. Include the SPDX header and the `phi^2 + 1/phi^2 = 3 | TRINITY` line top and bottom.

Declare `pub const AxiKind = enum(i8) { axi4_lite = 0, axi4_full = 1 }`, the channel codes CH_AW/CH_AR/CH_W/CH_R/CH_B as i8, MAX_BUS_PORTS, and the standard AXI signal widths as pub consts (addr 32, data 32, strb 4, id 4, len 8, size 3, burst 2, resp 2, cache 4, prot 3, qos 4, region 4, user 1).

Types: `AxiBusConfig` with name, kind, addr_width, data_width, id_width and the has_region / has_cache / has_prot / has_qos / has_user / has_lock flags; and a flat `BusPort` with name, direction, width and channel.

Constructors: axi4_lite_slave, axi4_lite_master, axi4_full_slave and axi4_full_master — Lite sets id_width 0 with only prot, Full sets region, cache, qos and lock. Queries: is_lite, is_full, strb_width (data_width/8) and is_master. Then `slave_port_count(cfg)` counting AW, W, B, AR and R channel ports conditionally on the optional signals, `total_bus_bits(cfg)`, and `validate_axi(cfg)` returning an error count for an empty name, zero address or data width, a data width not a multiple of 8, or a Full config with zero id_width.

Cover all of that with given/then tests, invariants tying strb_width to data_width and id_width to the kind, and nanosecond benches for validate and the port count.

Write a t27 spec in the module dialect, `module Assembler`, specifying the T27 ternary assembler that lowers the ternary ISA to machine code, including the GF16 extended instructions. Keep it parser-compatible with flat arrays and count fields. SPDX header, and the `phi^2 + 1/phi^2 = 3 | TRINITY` line at the top and as a trailing line after the module.

Enums as `pub const ... = enum(i8)`: SectionKind (text, data, bss, rodata) and RelocKind (abs32, rel21, gf16_label).

Structs: AssembledInstr (address, opcode, rd, rs1, rs2, imm, label, is_gf16), RelocEntry, Symbol (name, address, size, section, is_global) and AsmSection, plus AsmConfig with name, text_base, data_base, word_size and the has_gf16_ext / has_ternary_ext flags.

Constructors: asm_config defaulting text_base 0, data_base 4096, word_size 4 and both extensions on; text_section and data_section; r_instruction, i_instruction and gf16_instruction; symbol; reloc.

Queries and encoders: is_r_type, is_i_type, is_gf16_instr, encode_r_type packing opcode/rd/rs1/rs2 at shifts 26/21/16/11, encode_i_type packing a 16-bit immediate, section_end, align_address (identity when alignment is 0 or the address is already aligned), and instr_count. Validation: validate_config and validate_symbol returning error counts for empty names and a zero word size.

Then the TDD section in given/then form covering every constructor, both encoders, all three align_address branches, instr_count, and both validators on good and bad input. Add invariants for a positive word size, data_base at or above text_base, align_address never decreasing an address, and a non-negative error count, plus a nanosecond bench for encode_r_type.

Write a t27 spec in the module dialect, `module Power`, that specifies power estimation for T27 FPGA designs against an Artix-7 model. Document the model in the header: LUT 10 uW/MHz, FF 5, BRAM 50, DSP 100, IO 20, static 50 mW base plus 0.1 uW per resource unit. Keep it parser-compatible (flat arrays, count fields), SPDX header, and the `phi^2 + 1/phi^2 = 3 | TRINITY` line top and bottom.

Types: `pub struct PowerDomain` with name, voltage_mv, clock_mhz and toggle_rate, built by `power_domain(name, clock_mhz)` defaulting to 1000 mV and a toggle rate of 12; and `pub struct PowerEstimate` with dynamic_mw, static_mw, total_mw and the four per-resource microwatt fields, built by `power_estimate(dynamic, static)` and `zero_power()`.

Expose each model coefficient as its own nullary function. Then specify est_lut_dynamic and est_ff_dynamic (resource count x coefficient x clock x toggle rate, scaled down by 1000 and 100), est_bram_dynamic and est_dsp_dynamic (no toggle factor), est_static, total_resources, and est_total_power which combines them all into a filled PowerEstimate. Add `validate_domain` returning an error count for an empty name or a zero clock.

Write the TDD section in given/then form: the two constructors and zero_power, each estimator (with est_bram_dynamic(10, 100) == 50 and est_dsp_dynamic(8, 100) == 80 pinned exactly), est_static at zero equalling the base, total_resources(1000, 2000, 10, 8) == 3018, a full Arty-scale estimate where the total exceeds both components, the constant values, and validate_domain on good, empty-name and zero-clock inputs. Add invariants for non-negative power and a positive static base, plus a sub-100ns bench for est_total_power.

Write a t27 spec in the module dialect, `module FormulaDiscovery`, for the v1.0 ULTRA ENGINE formula-search layer. Import math::constants. Use the SPDX header and the `φ² + 1/φ² = 3 | TRINITY` banner.

First declare the sacred constants PHI, PI and E to 17 significant digits. Then declare, as f64 consts, the base formulas carried over from formula_registry.t27 that act as parents for chimera search: S1_gamma = phi^-3; PM1b_alpha_inv_exact = 360/phi^2 - 2/phi^3 + 1/(3phi)^5; N1_alpha_s = 1/(phi^4 + phi); N2_Tc; the CKM entries theta_C and V_cb; the PMNS entries sin2th23, delta_CP and sin2th12; and H1_mH_mZ. Follow them with the chimera v07 batch P10 through P18 (V_ud, V_cs, V_td, a sin2th12 variant, delta_CP in radians, ms/mmu, mb/mt, Omega_b and n_s), each as a phi/pi/e monomial.

Then the search primitives: chimera_mul, chimera_div (guarding |b| < 1e-15), chimera_add, chimera_sub, chimera_sin, chimera_cos, chimera_ln (guarding x <= 0), chimera_exp, chimera_pow, and `generate_basis(max_pow)` which enumerates n·φ^i·π^j·e^k over the cube of exponents and returns labelled values.

Close with a TDD section: given/and/when/then tests verifying S1_gamma, N1_alpha_s and PMNS2_sin2th23 against their PDG values to within 0.1 percent relative error, plus the trinity identity phi^2 + 1/phi^2 = 3 to 1e-12; and named invariant blocks asserting phi is between 1.5 and 1.7, gamma is in (0,1), sin2th23 is in (0,1), and the CKM entries used are positive with V_ud below 1.

Write a t27 spec in the module dialect, `module BootROM`, specifying the T27 boot ROM: boot stages, init vectors and an integrity checksum. Keep it parser-compatible using flat arrays plus explicit count fields, and note that in the header. SPDX line first, `phi^2 + 1/phi^2 = 3 | TRINITY` at the top of the banner and as a trailing comment after the module.

Types: `pub struct BootStage` with name, index, size_bytes and entry_addr, plus a `boot_stage(name, idx, size, entry)` constructor and `stage_end(s)` returning entry_addr + size_bytes; and `pub struct BootConfig` with name, rom_base, rom_size, has_integrity_check and has_chain_loader, built by `boot_config(name, rom_size)` which bases the ROM at 0 and turns both features on.

Functions: `validate_config(cfg)` returning a count of errors for an empty name or a zero ROM size; `config_end(cfg)`; and `fits(cfg, stages, count)` which sums the stage sizes over the first `count` entries and reports whether they fit inside rom_size.

Then a TDD section written in the `test <name> / given / and / then` form, covering: stage and config construction; validate_config on a good config, on a struct literal with an empty name, and on a zero size; fits returning true for two stages inside 8192, false for one 4096-byte stage in 1024, true for an exact fit and true for an empty stage list; stage_end on a non-zero entry address; and contiguous indexing where stage_end(s0) equals s1's entry_addr. Add an invariant that a constructed config has a positive ROM size, and a bench measuring `fits` against a sub-100ns target.

Write a t27 testbench spec in the module dialect, `module APB_Bridge_Testbench`, that exercises the APB bus protocol — setup phase, access phase and wait states — against fpga::apb_bridge::ApbBridge. SPDX header plus the `phi^2 + 1/phi^2 = 3 | TRINITY` banner line.

Constants: CLK_PERIOD 20, SIM_TIMEOUT 5_000_000, APB_ADDR_WIDTH 12, APB_DATA_WIDTH 32.

Declare module-level `var` signals modelling the bus: clk, rst_n, psel, penable, pwrite, paddr, pwdata, prdata, pready, pslverr, plus test_passed and test_failed counters.

Helpers: `tick()` toggling the clock low then high; `reset()` holding rst_n low for two ticks and releasing it; `apb_write(addr, data) -> bool` driving the setup phase (psel high, penable low), then the access phase (penable high), spinning on `while !pready { tick(); }`, deasserting, and returning `!pslverr`; and `apb_read(addr) -> u32` following the same two-phase handshake and latching prdata.

Write the tests as `test <name> { ... }` blocks whose assertions are `invariant <expr>;` statements: reset state, a single write, a single read, a write/read round trip at 0x200 with 0xCAFEBABE, eight sequential writes at word-aligned addresses read back and compared, and an explicit walk through the setup and access protocol phases. Add module-level invariants that the address width is positive and the data width is exactly 32, and a bench that resets and then performs 64 writes followed by 64 reads.

Write a t27 testbench spec in the module dialect, `module Assembler_Testbench`, covering ternary instruction encoding, program assembly and memory linking. It depends on fpga::assembler::Assembler and fpga::linker::Linker. Use the SPDX header and the `phi^2 + 1/phi^2 = 3 | TRINITY` banner.

Constants: CLK_PERIOD 20, INSTR_WIDTH 32, DATA_WIDTH 32, ADDR_WIDTH 16, MAX_PROGRAM_SIZE 1024, NUM_REGISTERS 8.

Declare module-level `var` signals for the DUT interface — clk, rst_n, instr_in, instr_out, addr_in, data_out, assemble_valid, link_done, link_error — plus test_passed and test_failed counters.

Helpers: `tick()` and `reset()` in the usual two-tick form; `encode_r_type(opcode, rd, rs1, rs2) -> u32` packing the fields at bit offsets 0, 8, 12 and 16; `encode_i_type(opcode, rd, rs, imm) -> u32` with the 16-bit immediate at offset 16; and the decoders `decode_opcode` (low byte) and `decode_rd` (nibble at offset 8).

Write the checks as `test <name> { ... }` blocks whose assertions are `invariant <expr>;` statements: the reset state leaves assemble_valid and link_done low; an encoded R-type round-trips through decode_opcode and decode_rd; the same for an I-type; and the program-size, register-count and instruction-width constants hold. Add module-level invariants that MAX_PROGRAM_SIZE and NUM_REGISTERS are positive, and a bench that encodes 100 R-type and 100 I-type instructions with rotating register indices.

Write a t27 testbench spec in the module dialect, `module VcdConformanceCompare_Testbench`, exercising the conformance comparison engine from fpga::vcd_conformance_compare — batch compare, masking and value extraction. SPDX header and the `phi^2 + 1/phi^2 = 3 | TRINITY` banner line.

Constants: CLK_PERIOD 20 and MAX_COMPARES 128. Module-level `var` state: clk, rst_n, compare_en, total_checks, pass_count, fail_count, plus test_passed and test_failed counters.

Helpers: `tick()` toggling the clock; `reset()` which pulses rst_n and then zeroes total_checks, pass_count and fail_count; and `run_compare(vcd: [u32], vcd_count: u32, expected_vals: [u32], expected_count: u32) -> u32` which walks the expected values and counts positions where the index is within vcd_count and the two values are equal.

Write the checks in two styles, as the file mixes them: a `test` block using `invariant <expr>;` assertions to show reset clears all three counters, and `test` blocks in the `given / and / then` form for run_compare — all three values matching returns 3, one mismatch returns 2, no matches returns 0, empty inputs return 0, and a vcd slice shorter than the expected list returns only the matching prefix. Add tests pinning MAX_COMPARES and CLK_PERIOD, a module-level invariant that MAX_COMPARES is positive, and a bench that enables compare_en and runs 100 ticks.

Write a t27 spec in the module dialect, `module PellisVerify`, for phase 2 of the GF competitive analysis (issue #289): GMP-backed high-precision verification of the Pellis closed form for the inverse fine-structure constant. Import base::types. SPDX header, and note the file purpose plus the TRINITY identity line in the banner.

Constants as f64: CODATA_ALPHA_INV = 137.035999166, PELLIS_PRELIMINARY = 137.035999164, and VERIFICATION_TOLERANCE = 0.001.

Two functions. `pellis_closed_form(phi_sq, phi_4, phi_5_3) -> f64` computes 360/phi^2 - 2/phi^4 + 1/(3*phi)^5 from the three precomputed powers passed in; put the formula in a comment above it. `compare_with_codata(pellis) -> f64` returns the relative error against CODATA_ALPHA_INV, guarding a zero denominator and taking the absolute difference by hand rather than calling out to a math library.

Write the TDD section with `test <name> { ... }` blocks that bind the three phi powers as f64 vars (phi^2 = 2.618033988749895, phi^4 = 6.854101966249685, (3phi)^5 = 44.322849) and use `try <condition>;` assertions: one test that the relative error is under VERIFICATION_TOLERANCE, and one sanity test that the result exceeds 137. Add an invariant that the preregistered preliminary value lies strictly between 137.035 and 137.036, an invariant that CODATA_ALPHA_INV is positive, and a bench block that evaluates the closed form.

Write a t27 spec in the module dialect, `module automation::wrapup`, for Ring-071 RAG-backed semantic memory: the `tri wrapup` command that pushes a session summary into NotebookLM. It imports memory::notebooklm. Start with the SPDX line, then `#`-style comment lines naming the file, the ring and the `phi^2 + 1/phi^2 = 3 | TRINITY` identity.

Constants: DEFAULT_NOTEBOOK = "t27-QUEEN-BRAIN" and VENV_PATH = ".trinity/notebooklm-venv". Add comments recording that the command is `tri wrapup`, that it is invoked from Claude Code via `/tri wrapup` or the Skill tool, and that the backend lives at contrib/backend/notebooklm/wrapup_auto.py.

Declare `struct WrapUpInput` with summary, decisions, a files_modified string list, next_steps, session_id, and the GitHub issue_number and issue_title (comment the last two). Declare `struct WrapUpResult` with notebook_id, notebook_name, source_id and uploaded_at, and note in a comment that notebook_name has the shape "t27 #NNN -- title".

Describe `wrapup_run(input: WrapUpInput) -> (WrapUpResult, ErrorCode)` in a comment as finding or creating the notebook, formatting markdown and uploading the source; it needs no body.

Finish with a single `test "wrapup_run_uploads_source"` block that builds a WrapUpInput literal for issue 350 titled "NotebookLM Integration", destructures the returned tuple, and asserts the error is ErrorCode::Success, that source_id is non-empty, and that notebook_name equals "t27 #350 -- NotebookLM Integration".

Write a t27 spec in the module dialect, `module TernaryControlFlow`, for Ring 090: control flow on the ternary architecture — conditional jumps, branches, and call/return. Import base::types. SPDX header plus the `phi^2 + 1/phi^2 = 3 | TRINITY` line.

Constants: the trit values TRIT_NEG -1, TRIT_ZERO 0, TRIT_POS 1; the condition codes COND_EQ 0, COND_NE, COND_POS, COND_NEG, COND_NZ, COND_NC 5 (always true); and the prediction hints PRED_TAKEN, PRED_NOT_TAKEN, PRED_NONE.

Stack forms: `call(addr, sp, memory: []TernaryWord) -> bool` pushing the return address with stack-overflow and bounds checks, and `ret_pop(sp, memory) -> bool`. Write the TDD section in `given / and / then` style covering each condition code, both branch helpers, relative jumps forward and backward (including the wrap to 0xFFFFFFFF), all three compare outcomes, both table_branch paths, and link-register save and restore. Close with nanosecond benches for each operation.

Write a t27 spec in the module dialect, file-scoped `module lsp-protocol;`, mapping LSP onto JSON-RPC 2.0 transport. Import usize from tritype-base. SPDX header and the `φ² + 1/φ² = 3 | TRINITY` banner.

Constants: JSON_RPC_VERSION, DEFAULT_BUFFER_SIZE 4096, MAX_MESSAGE_LENGTH 10485760, and the fifteen method-name constants from initialize through textDocument/rename — declare them as `[]const u8`, not fixed-size arrays.

Two design points must be honoured and explained in doc comments where they occur. First, MessageBuffer's `data` is `[]u8`, not `[]const u8` — a buffer whose bytes cannot be written is not a buffer, and the earlier shape paired a mutable-sounding `capacity` with an immutable empty slice, so it claimed room for 1024 bytes while holding none. Close with `@compileAssert` invariants for the version string and the enum ranges, and 1000-iteration benches for the cheap constructors.
